The Order page at http://localhost:3000/ is reached directly with no credential prompt, no Authorization header, and no session cookie observed in recording.har. Per scope, authentication_required is not set, so this is treated as unknown/out-of-scope rather than a finding.

findings.title: Order approval workflow: repeated Request-price-adjustment calls may pay out the $30 adjustment more than once
findings.evidence: Draft plan mutations/return-demo/01_replay_price_adjustment_twice.plan.json: resets the demo order, then calls POST /api/order/price-adjustment twice in a row. The UI hides the 'Request price adjustment' button and the recorded response moves priceProtection.status from 'eligible' to 'completed' after one call (recording.har entries 0-1), but this only proves the CLIENT stops offering the action — it does not prove the SERVER rejects a second call. Awaiting backend execution to confirm whether order.totalReturned exceeds order.originalAmount ($100) after the second call.

findings.title: Order approval workflow: three rapid repeats of Request-price-adjustment stress single-use enforcement beyond a simple replay
findings.evidence: Draft plan mutations/return-demo/02_repeat_price_adjustment_three_times.plan.json calls the same endpoint three times sequentially after a fresh reset, checking whether any per-request (rather than per-order) idempotency guard lets totalReturned exceed originalAmount. Awaiting backend execution.

findings.title: Price-adjustment endpoint may trust client-supplied amount fields instead of recomputing them server-side
findings.evidence: The recorded happy-path call sent an empty body (bodySize 0; recording.har entry 1) and the server still computed adjustmentAmount=30 itself, which is a good sign. Draft plan 03 resends the call with adjustmentAmount/totalReturned/netCustomerBenefit set to 9999 to check whether an alternate code path reads these from the body. Awaiting backend execution.

findings.title: Price-adjustment endpoint accepts a body containing unrelated privilege/status fields (status, isAdmin, verified, role) not sent by the UI
findings.evidence: Draft plan 04 posts status/isAdmin/verified/role/priceProtection.status overrides. This is a field-acceptance claim (not an amount bound), so it is declared unsupported_business_rule for the automated invariant check; the raw before/after order object still needs manual comparison once executed to confirm none of these keys were persisted.

verification.unsupported_reason: Field-acceptance/mass-assignment cannot be expressed as sum_lte; requires manual diff of before/after order object per injected key.

findings.title: Price-adjustment endpoint may mishandle malformed/extreme numeric or type-confused input (negative amount, float quantity, string amount)
findings.evidence: Draft plan 05 sends adjustmentAmount=-5000, quantity=0.5, totalReturned='unlimited' in the body. Awaiting backend execution to confirm totalReturned still respects originalAmount despite the malformed input.

findings.title: Second price-adjustment call attempts to forge priceProtection.status back to 'eligible' to re-arm the payout
findings.evidence: Draft plan 06 calls the endpoint once normally, then again with a body claiming priceProtection.status='eligible', adjustmentAmount=0 to see if the server trusts the client's claimed prior state rather than its own stored order state. Awaiting backend execution.

findings.title: Potential double-reimbursement across price adjustment, order cancellation, and refund actions could not be tested — the cancel/refund endpoints were never recorded
findings.evidence: The Order page shows 'Request refund' and 'Cancel order' buttons co-visible with 'Request price adjustment' in the very first UI state (demo.json workflow_timeline.ui_states[0]), and the GET /api/order response contains cancellation.reimbursementAmount, refund.status/requestedAmount/completedAmount, and availableActions.cancelOrder/requestRefund/completeRefund fields (recording.har entry 0) that are never exercised by this recording. Their backing endpoints (e.g. POST /api/order/cancel, /api/order/refund/request, /api/order/refund/complete) are absent from endpoint_catalog.json, so the backend will not authorize probing them from this run.

execution.missing_precondition: Cancel order, Request refund, and Complete refund endpoints were never invoked during recording and have no configured_setup/validated_recording entry in endpoint_catalog.json.
execution.next_step: Record a second pass of this flow that clicks 'Cancel order' and 'Request refund' (and, if a staff view exists, 'Complete refund'), then re-run Analyst/Saboteur so these become validated endpoints. Specifically verify server-side that cancellation.reimbursementAmount + priceProtection.adjustmentAmount + refund.completedAmount can never sum above order.originalAmount, and that cancelOrder/requestRefund are rejected once priceProtection.status is 'completed' (matching the client-side gating already observed).
